subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Current is an SI base quantity and its base unit is the ampere (A). The coulomb (charge), volt (p.d.) and ohm (resistance) are derived units.

questions.q: A permanent magnet is one that:
options: Only becomes magnetic when near another magnet
Produces its own magnetic field all the time
questions.explain: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field continuously.

questions.q: A converging lens brings parallel rays of light together. The point where they meet is called the:
questions.explain: A converging (convex) lens refracts parallel rays so they meet at the principal focus (focal point). The distance from the lens to this point is the focal length.

questions.q: A coil rotates steadily in a magnetic field. At which position is the induced p.d. greatest?
options: When the coil is perpendicular to the field lines
When the coil is parallel to the field lines, cutting them fastest
questions.explain: The induced p.d. is largest when the coil cuts field lines at the greatest rate. This occurs as the coil moves parallel to the field lines, and is zero when it momentarily moves along the lines without cutting them.

questions.q: Two magnets are placed near each other. Which pairing will REPEL?
options: A magnet near an unmagnetised iron nail
questions.explain: Like poles repel, so two north poles push apart. Unlike poles (N–S) attract, and an unmagnetised iron nail is always attracted (induced magnetism).

questions.q: What are the frequency and potential difference of the UK mains supply?
questions.explain: The UK mains supply is alternating current (ac) at a frequency of 50 Hz and a potential difference of about 230 V.

questions.q: Why is the field of a solenoid similar to that of a bar magnet?
options: Because the current flows in a circle only once
Because the fields from each loop add up to give a strong uniform field inside and a bar-magnet field outside
Because the wire is made of iron
questions.explain: The circular fields from each turn combine to give a strong, nearly uniform field inside the solenoid and an external field shaped like that of a bar magnet, with a north and south end.

questions.q: How could you reverse the direction of the force on a wire in an electric motor?
options: Reverse the direction of the current
questions.explain: Reversing the current (or the magnetic field) reverses the direction of the force.

questions.q: How can you reverse the direction of the force on a wire in an electric motor?
options: By reversing either the current OR the magnetic field direction
It is impossible to reverse the force
Only by switching off the current
questions.explain: Reversing the current direction or the magnetic field direction reverses the force. (Reversing both at once returns the force to its original direction.)

questions.q: A step-up transformer:
questions.explain: A step-up transformer increases the voltage and decreases the current (power is conserved).

questions.q: What happens to parallel rays of light after they pass through a converging (convex) lens?
options: They are brought together at the principal focus
They are absorbed by the lens
They spread out as if from a point behind the lens
questions.explain: A converging lens refracts parallel rays so that they meet at the principal focus (focal point). A diverging lens, by contrast, spreads parallel rays out.

questions.q: Which component is represented by a circle with a cross inside it?
questions.explain: A filament lamp is shown as a circle with a cross inside. A diode is a triangle pointing to a line, and a fuse is a rectangle with a line through it.

questions.q: In a UK three-pin plug, what colour is the live wire?
questions.explain: The live wire is brown, the neutral wire is blue, and the earth wire is green and yellow striped. The live wire alternates between a high positive and negative potential.

questions.q: The motor effect occurs when:
options: A current-carrying wire is placed in a magnetic field and experiences a force
questions.explain: The motor effect is the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.

questions.q: An alternator produces:
questions.explain: An alternator uses slip rings to produce an alternating current.

questions.q: What happens to the induced potential difference if the direction in which a magnet moves through a coil is reversed?
questions.explain: Reversing the motion (or the magnet's poles) reverses the direction of the induced p.d. This is why a coil rotating in a field produces alternating current.

questions.q: What did the alpha particle scattering experiment lead Rutherford to conclude?
options: Atoms are a ball of positive charge with electrons embedded in it
Mass and positive charge are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus
Electrons orbit at fixed distances in shells
questions.explain: Most alpha particles passed straight through but a few were deflected back, showing the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus — replacing the plum pudding model.

questions.q: In a simple generator, a larger induced voltage can be produced by:
questions.explain: Rotating the coil faster increases the rate of change of the field, increasing the induced voltage.

questions.q: The force between an induced magnet and the magnet that induces it is always:
questions.explain: Induced magnetism always produces a force of attraction towards the inducing magnet.

questions.q: When a current flows through a straight wire, it produces:
options: A magnetic field in circles around the wire
questions.explain: A current-carrying wire creates a circular magnetic field around it.

questions.q: An atom is electrically neutral. This is because it has an equal number of...
options: neutrons and protons in the nucleus only
questions.explain: Atoms are neutral because they contain equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons, so the charges cancel.

questions.q: Which change would NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet (solenoid)?
options: Using a thicker plastic former with no iron
questions.explain: Electromagnet strength increases with more current, more turns and an iron core. A plastic former with no iron does not boost the field.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625) syllabus; Electricity Magnetism
